A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MemoryAgentBench. Their main text, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched despite renumbering and additions.

before.justification: V2 reports original agent evaluations, ablations, latency measurements and GPU-memory results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains these empirical results and adds zero-shot, token-budget and overwrite-policy experiments in Appendices H, J and K.

M1.justification: The incremental memory-construction procedure and evaluated agent architectures are retained. V3's explanation of memorization instructions and newest-fact priority matches v2's existing Figures 4–5; the additional overwrite policies are experimental ablations.

E1.justification: The evaluated datasets and four competency categories remain unchanged. The new studies use existing classification, recommendation, summarization and FactConsolidation tasks; the additional benchmarks discussed in Table 1 are related-work comparisons, not newly evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: The evaluated model and agent roster is retained, including the membership of the main performance comparison. The additional studies vary history access, token budgets and prompts for existing comparators rather than adding another agent architecture or comparison method.

E3.justification: V3 adds no-history TTL evaluation and token-budget-controlled comparisons at approximately 4K, 40K and over 100K tokens. Appendix J uses GPT-4.1-mini across architectures and a random 30-book summarization subset; Appendix K introduces two overwrite-prompt conditions. These are substantial additional controls, while the original benchmark settings remain retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v3 tests dependence on historical examples, whether information budgets explain architectural differences, and sensitivity to aggressive versus conservative overwrite instructions. Appendix I also adds monetary cost–performance analysis alongside the existing latency and GPU-memory analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation run counts, actual seeds, confidence intervals or statistical tests. V3 promises future generation scripts with seeds, but supplies no new uncertainty estimates or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged, but Tables 16, 18 and 19 add substantial results under new conditions. For example, high-budget summarization on the 30-book subset scores 39.7, 38.0 and 38.8 for long-context, BM25 and MIRIX respectively. Table 19 reports FC-SH/FC-MH scores of 40.0/4.0 and 28.0/4.0 for the new policies versus 36.0/5.0 for the baseline. Table 17 adds estimated costs alongside reused performance scores.

T1.justification: The dataset notation and competency definitions are retained, with no added mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs. The new theoretical-necessity and task-rationale passages are conceptual arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: a unified four-competency benchmark, two newly constructed datasets, an evaluation framework and persistent weaknesses in existing memory agents.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands explanations of synthetic forgetting, the simplified two-stage TTL protocol, judging validity and chunked inputs. It adds cost and prompt-policy interpretations. Appendix J attributes summarization success chiefly to sufficient information access, introducing a qualification that is not reconciled with Section 4.2's retained account of fundamental architectural limitations.

D1.justification: V3 documents exact overwrite-policy prompts, cost-estimation prices and caching assumptions, and settings for the added controls. New statements specify intended MIT/CC BY 4.0 licensing and planned reproducibility artifacts. Existing code/data links and implementation details are retained; the PDFs do not establish delivery of the promised containers or seeds.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 expands into long-context, RAG and memory-agent benchmark categories, adding works including KILT, BEIR, LaRA, FRAMES and several other RAG benchmarks. New Table 1 compares competency and agent coverage, including MemoryBank and PerLTQA. The earlier categorical statement that no prior work repurposed long-context benchmarks for memory agents is removed.

P1.justification: V3 reorganizes and expands the benchmark-related-work discussion, adds a prompt-protocol explanation and disclosure statements, and introduces substantial explanatory appendices on task rationale, TTL design, judging and input format. This materially expands the document's explanatory structure, although the abstract, main experimental narrative and original appendices largely retain their wording.

P2.justification: V3 adds a benchmark-coverage matrix in Table 1 and four dedicated tables presenting zero-shot, cost, token-budget and overwrite-policy comparisons. These substantially expand the displayed evidence. The five existing figures and original tables are retained, with table renumbering and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new budget and overwrite controls address confounds left untested in v2 and improve the benchmark's diagnostic value. However, Table 16's Banking77 description conflicts with its reused aggregate MCC score, and its accuracy caption conflicts with recommendation Recall@5. Appendix J's information-access interpretation also remains unreconciled with Section 4.2's broad architectural claims. These reporting and interpretation issues limit the overall gain.
